To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the photoisomerization quantum yield is intrisically limited by stimulated emission and internal conversion and that the quantum yield is further limited by competing multi photon processes.

photoisomerisation in PYP is limited by ultrafast internal conversion as well as stimulated emission, multi-photon processes at 400 and 490 nm, and that the photochemical limit for quantum yield is 0.14 - 0.19.

the photochemical efficiency of PYP depends on peak power, that it is limited by ultrafast internal conversion, that it is further significantly limited with excitation at 450 nm by multi-photon processes into excited state absorption and that it is further limited with excitation wavelengths at 400 and 490 nm by stimulated emission.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental understanding of ultrafast photoisomerisation in the photoactive yellow proteins (PYP).
the fundamental understanding of the photochemical quantum yields of PYP and their dependence on pulse duration and excitation wavelength.
a detailed understanding of the ultrafast excited-state dynamics of PYP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

with excitation wavelengths of 400 nm and 450 nm, photoisomerisation is predominantly a one-photon process with quantum yields that are limited by ultrafast internal conversion, whereas with excitation at 450 nm the photoisomeration quantum yield is additionally limited by stimulated emission and with excitation at longer wavelengths by stimulated emission and excited state absorption.

with 450 nm femtosecond laser excitation the photoisomerization quantum yield of PYP is not limited by stimulated emission or multi-photon excitaion but is limited by the ultrafast internal conversion process.
the photochemical reaction of PYP with femtosecnd pulses is not a single photon process but rather a multi-photon process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

femtosecond pulse durations are beneficial to increase the quantum yield of photochemical processes, but only if the stimulated emission cross-section of the first excited electronic state is significantly smaller than the ground state absorption cross-section.

the quantum yield for photoisomerization of PYP is limited by the competition between stimulated emission and ultrafast internal conversion, and that this limit is further reduced by multi-photon exciation.
the quantum yield for photoisomerization in PYP with 150 fs pulses and 450 nm exciation is 0.14, the quantum yield for excited state absorption is 0.86 and the excited state cross-section is 0.36.
The main takeaway from our work is that

femtosecond laser excitation can be used as a tool to study the excited state dynamics of PYP in a wide variety of conditions and to determine the underlying quantum yield of photochemical processes in PYP.
femtosecond pulse duration is not a panacea to avoid multi-photon processes in photochemistry.

the quantum yield of photochemical reactions can be significantly affected by ultrafast excited state dynamics and stimulated emission. The latter can be further enhanced by increasing pulse durations, and the former can be reduced by increasing pulse duration.
